name: 20 dominoes
description: 20 dominoes can refer to domino games played with a 20-tile set or scoring to 20. When played as a Blackjack-style game, it is similar to Twenty-One dominoes: players draw tiles aiming for a total of 20 or 21 without busting, with a banker.

overview.description: 20 dominoes can refer to domino games played with a 20-tile set or scoring to 20. When played as a Blackjack-style game, it is similar to Twenty-One dominoes: players draw tiles aiming for a total of 20 or 21 without busting, with a banker.

history.origins: Domino banking game; aim for 20 or 21 (like blackjack) vs banker. Tiles drawn, pip total; blank often 0 or 7. Payout may multiply by tiles in hand (e.g. squared).
timeline: Modern era: described in Western sources as a blackjack-style domino banking game using a double-six set and aiming for totals of 20 or 21 against a banker.
history.cultural: Domino variant of twenty-one style play.

setup.dealing: Banker chosen (e.g. by drawing highest tile). Players buy tiles from the banker for a stake; max nine tiles per hand.
setup.equipment: Double-six domino set, chips or stakes

rules.objective: Reach a total of 20 or 21 (or as close as possible without busting) to beat the banker. Stick to stop; bust if over 21 and lose the wager.
rules.gameplay: Players take turns buying tiles from the banker, keeping a running total. Beyond the first two tiles, one tile is turned face-up so each player has two face-down and the rest face-up. Stick to stop; bust if over 21. Banker then draws without exceeding 21; banker bust pays all remaining players; otherwise banker collects from lower or equal totals and pays higher.
keyRules: Banker draws last; settles with each player

strategy.basic: Stop when you are close to 21 and the banker may bust; avoid taking tiles that risk busting. Remember blank can be 0 or 7 to flex your total.
strategy.intermediate: Consider how many tiles the banker has drawn and visible totals; more tiles in your hand multiplies payout (squared) so sometimes taking one more tile is worth the bust risk.
strategy.advanced: Double-blank + one tile for exactly 21 with three tiles beats everything; aim for that when the stake is high.
tips: Blank counts 0 or 7—use it to land on 20 or 21.
21 with exactly three tiles including double-blank beats the banker even if banker has 21.
Payout is stake × (tiles in hand)²—more tiles = much higher payoff.
Stick when your total is strong and banker might bust.

scoring.description: Reach 20 or 21 without busting; banker settles winnings.
scoring.winCondition: First to 20 or 21 without exceeding beats banker.
